Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan, Senior Advocate instructed by Nurul Islam Bhuiyan, Advocate-on-Record ----- For the Appellant 
A. J. Mohammad Ali, Senior Advocate, instructed by Mrs. Sufia Khatun, Advocate-on-Record ----- For Respondent No. 1

Vs.
Mohammad Humayun being dead his legal heirs: 1(a). Abdur Rashid and others ----- Respondents
case_source: (From the Judgment and order dated 29.01.2006 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 504 of 2001)
full_judgment:
Nazmun Ara Sultana J.:- This Civil Appeal, by leave granted in Civil Review Petition No. 16 of 2008, has arisen from the judgment and order dated 29.01.2006 passed by a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 504 of 2001 making the rule absolute and thereby setting aside the judgment and decree dated 17.09.2000 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka in Title Appeal No. 218 of 1992 affirming those dated 25.06.1992 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 4th Artha Rin Adalat, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 72 of 1992 dismissing the suit.

<u>2. Mohammad Humayun-the predecessor of the present plaintiff-respondents herein, as plaintiff; instituted Title Suit No. 224 of 1984 in the 3rd Court of the Sub-judge, Dhaka which was subsequently transferred to the court of Sub-judge and 4th Artha Rin Adalat, Dhaka and was renumbered as Title Suit No. 72 of 1992, for declaration of title, recovery of khas possession and for further declaration to the effect that the expert decree passed in Title Suit No. 231 of 1977 of the 3rd Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka is illegal and not binding upon the plaintiff.</u>

3. The case of the plaintiff, in short, is that the suit property originally belonged to Hazi Abdul Wahab. Hazi Abdul Wahab transferred the suit property in favour of his second wife-who adopted Islam as religion from Hinduism and took the name Nurjahan Begum. The said Nurjahan Begum expressed her desire to take Abdur Rouf, a son of the plaintiff, as her son and Hazi. Abdul Wahab gave his consent to it. When said Abdur Rouf became adult he married a girl of a family of Tongi Area without the knowledge of his father and started living at the residence of his father-in-law and in the meantime Nurjahan Begum died in Dhaka Medical College Hospital on 28.08.1978 without any issue. As a result the heirs of Abdul Wahab got the suit property by the law of inheritance. But Abdur Rouf claimed the suit property on the ground that Nurjahan Begum before, her death, made a gift of the suit property in his favour for which the plaintiff Md. Humayun instituted Title Suit No. 167 of 1975 for partition Abdur Rouf also filed Title Suit No. 165 of 1975 claiming the suit property which was subsequently dismissed for default. The Title Suit No. 167 of 1975 filed by the plaintiff was decreed on compromise on 01.03.1999 and the plaintiff got the suit land in his shaham by the said compromise decree.

4. That Abdur Rouf-the proforma defendant No. 2 entered into an agreement for sale of the suit property with the defendant No. 1, on 09.02.1977 and subsequently the defendant No. 1 filed Title Suit No. 231 of 1977 for specific performance of contract against Abdur Rouf and that suit was decreed ex-parte and the defendant No. 1, by filing execution case, got the kabala deed executed and registered through court on 05.02.1979 Thereafter, the defendant No. 1 filed a suit for permanent injunction, that since the decree for specific performance of contract was passed during the pendency of Title Suit No. 167 of 1975 the said decree was barred by the principle of lies-pendency, moreover since the defendant No. 2 had no right, title and interest in the suit property, the defendant No. 1 also could not acquire any right, title and interest in the suit property by that decree That the defendant No. 1 dispossessed the plaintiff from the suit property in the middle of 1979 and hence the plaintiff has filed this suit

5. The defendant No 1 contested the suit by filing written statement denying the material allegations made in the plaint His defence case was that Abdul Wahab transferred the suit property in favour of Nurjahan Begum by executing a deed of lease and as Nurjahan Begum had no issue she brought up the proforma defendant No. 2-who had been living with' Nurjahan Begum in the suit property and Nurjahan Begum thereafter transferred the suit property by way of gift in favour of the proforma defendant No. 2 on 20.08.1970 and confirmed that oral gift by executing a written instrument on 23.08.1970 and subsequently died on 28.08.1978. That the plaintiff was fully aware of this fact and he attempted to dispossess the proforma defendant No. 2 from the suit property. The proforma defendant No. 2 then filed Title Suit No. 165 of 1975 for permanent injunction which was subsequently dismissed for non-prosecution. That the proforma defendant No. 2 executed a bainapatra in favour of the defendant No. 1 on 09.02.1977 by taking Tk. 50,000/- out of stipulated consideration of Tk. 80,000/- and handed over possession of the suit property to the defendant No. 1. But since the proforma defendant No. 2 failed to execute the sale deed as per bainapatra the defendant No.1 filed Title Suit No. 231 of 1977 for specific performance of contract and got decree and also the sale deed executed and registered through court and got possession also through court. That as the plaintiff attempted to dispossess the defendant No. 1 from the suit land the defendant No. 1 filed a suit against the plaintiff and obtained an order of temporary injunction. That the plaintiff filed a suit for partition and though all the defendants except the present proforma defendant No. 2 filed compromise petition in that suit but this proforma defendant No. 2 did not sign that compromise petition. That the plaintiff has no right, title interest and possession in the suit property and as such the suit is liable to be dismissed.

6. The trial court, on consideration of evidence adduced by both the parties, dismissed the suit. The appellate court below affirmed this judgment and decree of the trial court. The plaintiff then moved the High Court Division in revision being Civil Revision No. 504 of 2001 and obtained rule. A Single Bench of the High Court, ultimately, made that rule absolute and set aside the judgment and decree of the courts below and decreed the suit.

<u>7. The defendant No. 1 then moved the Appellate Division with a petition for leave to appeal being No. 502 of 2006 and by the judgment and order dated 18.11.2007 the Appellate Division dismissed that leave petition. Thereafter, the defendant-petitioner filed an application for review of the said judgment and order dated 18.11.2007 and the Appellate Division, after hearing both the parties, allowed that review petition and granted leave on consideration of the submission of the learned Counsel for the leave petitioner to the effect that both the courts of facts concurrently found that the plaintiff was never in possession of the suit property and could not prove his possession and alleged dispossession from the suit property and failed to establish his possession in the suit property within 12 years prior to the institution of the suit and as such the suit was barred by Limitation and rightly dismissed the suit but the High Curt Division acted in excess of its revisional Jurisdiction in decreeing the suit without reversing the concurrent findings of fact of the courts of facts on the question of limitation and without considering the provisions of law.</u>

8. Mr. Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan, the learned Senior Advocate for the defendant-appellant has made submissions to the effect that in this suit the plaintiff has totally failed to prove his possession in the suit land within 12 years prior to institution of the suit and as such the suit for declaration of title and recovery of possession was barred by limitation, that both the trial court and the appellate court below, on thorough examination of the evidence adduced by both the parties, rightly found that the plaintiff could not prove his possession in the suit land and also alleged dispossession therefrom and, therefore, rightly dismissed the suit; that the High Court Division acted in excess of its revisional jurisdiction in decreeing the suit without reversing these concurrent findings of the courts of facts on finding of any misreading or non-reading of the material evidence on record. The learned Counsel for the defendant-appellant has made submissions to the effect also that Civil Revision No. 504 of 2001 was decided by the High Court Division in the absence of the present appellant who was the present appellant-who was opposite party No. 1 in that civil revision; that no notice of that civil revision was served on the opposite party No. 1 of that civil revision and consequently the opposite party No. 1 (the present appellant) did not get any opportunity to contest the rule issued in that civil revision and as a result the High Court Division could not take the right decision and consequently made the rule absolute most unjustly; that the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division is not sustainable in law in view of the fact that the High Court Division did not advert to or reversed the concurrent findings of both the courts of facts. The learned Counsel has contended that both the courts of facts, on proper evaluation and appreciation of the evidence adduced by both the parties rightly found that the plaintiff could not prove his possession in the suit land within 12 years prior to the institution of the suit, but the High Court Division without taking into consideration these concurrent findings of the courts of facts made the rule absolute most unjustly and arbitrarily.

9. Mr. A. J. Mohammad Ali, the learned Senior Advocate for the plaintiff-respondent No. 1 has made submissions supporting the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division. The learned Counsel has argued that the very defence case that the suit property was transferred to Nurjahan Begum by its original owner Abdul Wahab by deed of lease dated 19.03.1958 is not acceptable at all that this alleged lease deed is void because it was created after 16th December, 1955 which is hit under section 75 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. The learned Advocate has contended that the said lease deed was a mere paper transaction only which was never acted upon; that the proforma defendant No. 2 Abdur Rouf also could not acquire any right, title or interest in the suit property by virtue of the alleged oral gift made by Nurjahan Begum in his favour. The learned Counsel has argued also that the plaintiff of the present suit filed Title Suit No. 167 of 1975 for partition of the suit property and that suit was decreed on compromise by a competent court of law and so long this decree stands the defendants of the present suit cannot claim any right, title and interest in the suit land. The learned Counsel has argued also that the plaintiff has proved by sufficient evidence that the defendant No.1 dispossessed him from the suit land forcibly after obtaining the decree for specific performance of contract in Title Suit No. 231 of 1977 and as such this suit is not barred by limitation at all. The learned Counsel has contended that both the trial court and the appellate court below committed wrong in making assessment of the evidence adduced by the parties and thus arrived at a wrong findings and decision that the High Court Division assessed the evidence on record and other facts and circumstances properly and thus came to the correct decision.

10. We have considered the submissions of the learned Advocates of both the sides and gone through the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division and also those of the courts below.

11. Admittedly, the suit land originally belonged to Hazi Abdul Wahab. It is also an admitted fact that Hazi Abdul Wahab transferred the suit land to his second wife Nurjahan Begum by a registered lease deed dated 19.03.1958. The plaintiff, in his very pleadings, has stated this fact and did not raise any question as to the validity of this lease deed. The plaintiff in his plaint, rather, has stated to the effect that since Nurjahan Begum died childless the suit property devolved upon the heirs of Abdul Wahab after her death. The plaintiff, admittedly, did not raise any question as to the validity of this lease deed before any court-either in the present suit-or in any other earlier suits. In this present appeal before this Division, for the first time, the plaintiff has raised this question as to the validity of the lease deed in favour of Nurjahan Begum. However, this is a question of law and as such we entertain this question and hold that this lease deed being created after 16th December, 1955 is hit under section 75A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and as such is not a valid one.

12. Now the question is whether Nurjahan Begum acquired title in the suit land by adverse possession on the basis of this invalid lease deed. It is plaintiff’s case that Nurjahan Begum was in possession of the suit land after having this alleged lease deed executed and registered in her favour on 19.03.1958 and remained in possession of the suit land till her death in the year 1978. Both the trail court and the appellate court below, on proper assessment of the evidence on record and the facts and circumstances, found that Nurjahan Begum was in possession of the suit property by exercising her own right and title thereon on the basis of this alleged lease deed till her death in the year 1978. So, Nurjahan Begum acquired title in the suit land by virtue of adverse possession for more than 12 years. The plaintiff himself has admitted in his very pleadings that Hazi Abdul Wahab the original owner of the suit land transferred the suit land to his 2nd wife Nurjahan Begum by a registered lease deed dated 19.03.1958 and after the death of Nurjahan Begum the heirs of Abdul Wahab got the suit land by virtue of inheritance. These very statements of the plaintiff himself prove sufficiently that Nurjahan Begum possessed the suit land by exercising her own right, title and interest thereon on the basis of this registered lease deed dated 19.03.1958 and in the circumstances Nurjahan Begum acquired title in the suit land by virtue of adverse possession for a long period of about 20 years. The plaintiff has claimed that after the death of Nurjahan Begum he along with other heirs of Hazi Abdul Wahab inherited the suit land. But this claim of the plaintiff is not acceptable at all. The plaintiff or other heirs of Hazi Abdul Wahab are not the heirs of Nurjahan Begum. So, at the death of Nurjahan Begum the question of acquisition of the suit property by the heirs of Hazi Abdul Wahab does not arise at all The present appellant, as defendant No.1, in the original suit, pleaded a case that Nurjahan Begum before her death gifted the suit land to Abdur Rouf a son of the plaintiff whom Nurjahan Begum adopted as a son. The plaintiff himself also has pleaded that Nurjahan Begum with the consent of her husband Abdul Wahab Look Abdur Rouf as her son and reared up him. The plaintiff though has pleaded a case that subsequently Abdur Rouf, after attaining his marriageable age, married a girl of Tongi Area and started levity in his father-in-law's house at Tongi, but this case of the plaintiff has not been substantiated. Rather we find that there are sufficient evidence to prove that Abdur Rouf used to reside with Nurjahan Begum till her death. However, admittedly the defendant No.1 filed a suit for specific performance of contract being Case No. 231 of 1977 against Abdur Rouf and got an ex-parte decree and in execution of that ex-parte decree he got the kabala deed executed and registered through court and also got delivery of possession of one of the rooms of the suit property through court. The contesting defendant has adduced some evidence to prove that Nurjahan Begum gifted the suit property to Abdur Rouf orally and Abdur Rouf used to possess that suit property on the basis of oral gift and Abdur Rouf subsequently transferred the possession of the suit land excepting one room only on the basis of bainapatra executed by him in favour of the defendant No. 1. The defendant No. 1 has also proved by adducing necessary papers that after getting the kabala deed executed and registered through court in respect of the suit property he mutated the suit land in his name and paid rent to the government and got rent receipts and he has constructed also a 7 storied building on the suit land.

13. The plaintiff though has claimed that he was in possession of the suit property within 12 years prior to institution of the suit, but this claim of the plaintiff even if taken as true, does not entitle the plaintiff to get the decree as prayed for. Because according to the own case of the plaintiff Nurjahan Begum was possessing the suit land till her death in 1978 and this suit was filed in 1984. So, the plaintiff, if at all, took possession of the suit property after the death of Nurjahan Begum he possessed the same only for 5/6 years before filing of this suit. Since we have already found that at the death of Nurjahan Begum the plaintiff could not acquire any right, title or interest in the suit property the alleged possession of the plaintiff in the suit property for 5/6 years only does not entitle him l to get a decree in this suit for declaration of title and recovery of possession.

14. Mr. A. J. Mohammad Ali. the learned Counsel for the plaintiff-respondent has argued also to the effect that since the plaintiff- respondent got a decree for partition in respect of the suit land in Title Suit No. 167 of 1975 from a competent court of law his claim of title in the suit property cannot be brushed asides. But we are unable to accept this argument also of the learned Counsel. We have already I found that Nurjahan Begum acquired valid title in the suit property by virtue of long possession of more than 12 years on the basis of an invalid registered lease deed. So, the plaintiff or other heirs of Hazi Abdul Wahab had no right, title and possession in the suit land. The Partition Suit being Title Suit No. 167 of 1975 was filed among the heirs of Abdul Wahab and it was decreed on compromise. The pro-forma defendant No. 2 Abdul Roof though was made a defendant in that partition suit, but admittedly, he was not made a party in that compromise petition and he did not sign that compromise petition. However, where the suit property belonged to Nurjahan Begum this Partition Suit No. 167 of 1975 filed among the heirs of Hazi Abdul Wahab and the decree thereof arc not of any value at all, rather this compromise decree is a nullity. On the basis of this compromise decree the plaintiff or any other of the parties of that compromise acquired no right, title and interest in the suit property and this compromise decree is not binding on Abdur Rouf also-who did not sign the compromise petition.

15. However, on careful scrutiny of the evidence on record we find that the trial court and the appellate court below, on correct evaluation and appreciation of the evidence on record, rightly found that the plaintiff never had/has any right title and possession in the suit land. The trial court, therefore, rightly dismissed the suit and the appellate court below rightly affirmed the judgment and decree of the trial court.

<u>16. The High Court Division has committed wrong in decreeing the suit of the plaintiff setting aside the concurrent findings and decision of the court of facts. The High Court Division appears to have decreed the suit holding it as not barred by limitation. The High Court Division made observations to the effect that according to the own case of the contesting defendant No.1 he got possession of the suit land partly in the year 1977 when the bainapatra was made and got possession of the rest of the suit land in the year 1979 through court in execution of the decree in Title Suit No. 231 of 1977 and that the present suit .was filed in the year 1984 and as such it was not barred by Limitation. Obviously, the High Court Division did not take into consideration at all the admitted fact that Hazi Abdul Wahab-the original owner of the suit land transferred the suit land to Nurjahan Begum by a registered deed of the year 1958 and since then Nurjahan Begum was in possession of the suit land by exercising her own right and title thereon and thus acquired good title in the suit land by virtue of adverse possession for about 20 years till her death and as such at the death of Nurjahan Begum the heris of Hazi Abdul Wahab including the plaintiff could not acquire any right, title arid interest in the suit land. Nurjahan Begum admittedly, died in the year 1978 and as such the plaintiff though adduced some evidence to prove that he possessed the suit land for some period after the death of Nurjahan Begum in the year 1978 but this fact does not entitle him to get a decree for declaration of title and khas possession. The High Court Division took into consideration the alleged sloe decree passed in Partition Suit No. 167 of 1975 and opined that by virtue of this decree the plaintiff has got the suit property in his share ignoring the fact altogether that the plaintiff and the other heirs of Hazi Abdul Wahab did not acquire any right, title and interest in the suit land at the death of Nurjahan Begum-who acquired valid right, title and interest in the suit land by virtue of long possession for more than 20 years on the basis of a registered lease deed, though invalid. The High Court Division's further findings that the decree passed in Title Suit No. 231 of 1977 for specific performance of contract is hit by section 52 of the Transfer of Property Act since it was obtained during pendency of the partition suit-also is not correct. Since the decree of the Partition Suit No. 167 of 1975 is a nullity, doctrine of lis-pendency will not hit the decree passed in Title Suit No. 231 of 1977.</u>

17. However, from the above discussion it is evident, that the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division has been erroneous and as such cannot be sustained in law.

18. In the circumstances this appeal succeeds.

19. Hence ordered that the appeal be allowed on contest against the respondent No. 1 and ex-parte against the rest without any order as to cost. The impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division he set aside and those of the appellate court below and the trial court be affirmed.

End.
